problem: The sentence says a second distance from another known point 'cuts that circle at one point'. Two circles with centres at the two known points generally intersect at two points, not one, so the geometry as stated is wrong and a student will believe two distances always give one answer.
fix: One distance from one known point places the new point on a circle around that point. A second distance from another known point cuts that circle at two points; a rough sketch of the site, or a third measurement, decides which of the two is the real point.

problem: The answer says the second independent measurement 'gives a unique position'. As with two distances, two loci can meet at two candidate positions, so 'unique' overstates it.
fix: Answer: One measurement leaves a locus of possible positions; a second independent measurement intersects that locus and narrows the position to one or two candidates, and a sketch or a third measurement settles which one it is.

problem: The text lists six purpose classes (topographic, cadastral, engineering, control, hydrographic, astronomical) but the tree shows only four, so a reader may think the other two do not belong to the classification.
fix: Add 'Hydrographic' and 'Astronomical' as children of 'By purpose', or add a note that the branch shows only the four common classes.
